title: The visible is built on the invisible: small, unseen acts of care compound into culture
summary: Cris Pop argues that team culture is built in the background, through small unrequested improvements done with care. He says leaders should notice and name that invisible work, because people rarely know their effort mattered unless told. Feedback should include what was done right, not only what to fix.

principles.text: Real change mostly happens in the background, through people choosing to do small things well with no audience.
principles.quote: But most of the time, real change happens in the background. It’s someone choosing to do something well, even when the only witness is their own integrity.

principles.text: Look for the small details. How small things get done, or don't, shows who you are as a team.
principles.quote: At Thunder, we’ve learned not to overlook the small details. In fact, we look for it. Because the way small things get done (or don’t) says everything about who we are.

principles.text: Small improvements made daily with care compound until they become the culture and the work.
principles.quote: Small improvements, made daily, with care.

principles.text: Don't assume people know their good work landed. Tell them you saw it and that it mattered.
principles.quote: But even the best of us forget to say the most obvious thing: “I saw what you did, and it mattered.”

principles.text: Feedback should celebrate what someone got right, not only point at what's missing or broken.
principles.quote: Where feedback includes not just what to fix, but what you got right.

principles.text: Work is really about building belonging and trust, earned by how people show up for each other in little ways.
principles.quote: We’re building a team where trust is earned by the way we show up for each other, again and again, in the little ways.
